meta.title: ScandWave Energy — A new approach to wave energy
meta.description: ScandWave Energy AB is developing a research-based wave energy concept — from simulation to verified prototype. Published in Polish Maritime Research, 2024.

hero.title: A new approach to
hero.lead: From scientific theory and CFD simulation — to validation in a relevant environment along Sweden's west coast.

resistance.heading: Ocean energy remains largely untapped.
resistance.body: Europe has over 100 GW of technical wave energy potential. Yet few concepts have crossed from simulation into verified application. At the same time, the need is growing for dispatchable, fossil-free baseload and for infrastructure that meets an increasingly exposed coastal climate. Energy is lost in what is never built.

shift.heading: The challenge is not the ocean.
shift.headingAccent: It is how we interact with it.
shift.body: A new concept — validated against experimental data through CFD methodology — demonstrates that kinetic energy in marine waves can be converted more efficiently than previously assumed.

westCoast.heading: Where the prototype will be tested.
westCoast.body: The Bohuslän coastline — from the Gothenburg archipelago up to Kosterhavet — offers high wave energy, established ports and close access to research infrastructure. This is where ScandWave's testbed is planned to be verified.

innovation.heading: A system, not a machine.
innovation.body: ScandWave converts wave motion into usable energy through a mechanical and system-based process, analysed using Computational Fluid Dynamics.

pillars.title: Hydrodynamic form
pillars.body: Geometry optimised against real wave behaviour via CFD simulation — seabed-fixed, sized for mid-range near-shore waves.

pillars.title: Concentrated energy transfer
pillars.body: A channel geometry concentrates the wave's kinetic energy into a mechanical chain designed for low loss and scalability.

pillars.title: Scalable architecture
pillars.body: Modular system logic from testbed to pilot — and onward as a hybrid module on the same offshore platform as wind and solar.

hybrid.heading: A hybrid system — not a stand-alone wave device.
hybrid.body: ScandWave combines wave motion with complementary renewables on a single offshore platform. The system is designed to co-operate with wind and solar, and to support marine industries along Sweden's west coast.

sectors.title: Hybrid energy
sectors.body: Wave energy combined with wind and solar on a shared offshore platform — lower balancing needs and more stable output.
sectors.differentiator: ScandWave targets the near-shore transition zone, where waves still carry ~80 % of their energy. The wave component is seabed-fixed, scales in smaller increments, and acts as a base-load complement to wind and solar on the same platform.

sectors.title: Marine aquaculture support
sectors.body: Stable, locally generated electricity for sustainable aquaculture, marine farming and coastal food production — aligned with FAO's work on sustainable aquatic food systems.
sectors.differentiator: Unlike diesel gensets or long grid runs — identified by the FAO as a bottleneck for sustainable aquatic food systems — ScandWave delivers electricity on-site. The wave component keeps pumps, sensors and cooling running even when wind and solar output are low.

sectors.title: Marine environment & biodiversity
sectors.body: Designed with respect to coastal ecosystems and biodiversity, informed by current evidence on the marine environmental effects of wave power.
sectors.differentiator: ScandWave builds on the knowledge base assembled by havet.nu on the marine effects of wave power. Its seabed-fixed design minimises surface disturbance, avoids moving parts in the water column where marine life is most sensitive, and can be removed without lasting seabed impact. The foundation concept is being studied in low-carbon marine concrete with a secondary artificial-reef function — so the infrastructure contributes to biodiversity rather than competing with it.

foundation.figuresIntro: Selected graphs from Abbas et al. (2024). Simulated pressure and moment over time are used to compare the device response with and without a hemispherical geometry — the basis for the continuing prototype sizing work.

figures.title: Pressure over time — with and without hemisphere
figures.caption: Time series of averaged pressure (p) at the device inlet. Comparing configurations with and without the hemispherical feature shows how the geometry stabilises the pressure signal and raises the effective mean pressure.

figures.title: Moment at outlet, middleplane and open sea (2.4–4.5 s)
figures.caption: Moment [N·m] measured at three sections — outlet, middleplane and open sea. The difference between sections reflects energy extraction along the device during a wave cycle.

figures.title: Moment in quasi-steady regime (10.4–13.2 s)
figures.caption: The same three sections in a later, settled time window. Used to estimate steady-state power take-off and mechanical loads for component sizing.

roadmap.heading: From theory to verified prototype.
roadmap.body: The project is structured in five development stages, from concept and simulation toward verified prototype and pilot. Current status: stages 1–2.

stages.title: Technical review
stages.body: Consolidation and review of existing research, simulations and design assumptions.

stages.title: Prototype definition
stages.body: Selection of test level, dimensioning and practical scope for prototype or testbed.

stages.title: Design & engineering
stages.body: Technical specifications, component needs, test logic and buildability assessment.

stages.title: Build & test
stages.body: Establishment of prototype/test environment and first practical tests.

stages.title: Analysis & continuation
stages.body: Evaluation, documented learnings, and decision on pilot or scale-up toward commercial phase.

partnership.heading: We are forming a focused consortium of partners.
partnership.body: ScandWave Energy AB initiates and leads the project together with an industrial co-applicant, project and funding support via Adect, and relevant test and research partners in later stages.
